review.tagline: Desktop app that runs CLI coding agents in parallel git worktrees
review.summary: Orca is a desktop app for macOS, Windows and Linux that runs terminal-based coding agents such as Claude Code, Codex and OpenCode side by side, each in its own git worktree. It adds split terminals, an embedded browser with element picking, diff annotation, GitHub and Linear task views, SSH worktrees and a scriptable CLI. An iOS and Android companion app monitors agents and sends follow-ups.
review.audience: Developers running several CLI coding agents in parallel on one repo
strengths: Works with any CLI agent that runs in a terminal, with 30+ listed
Each agent gets an isolated git worktree, so parallel results can be compared
Supports remote worktrees over SSH with auto-reconnect and port forwarding
Orca CLI lets agents script worktree creation and browser actions
weaknesses: Does not include a model or agent; agent CLIs are installed and authenticated separately
Mobile app needs pairing with a running desktop host
Ships daily, so the README feature list lags behind the changelog
Collects anonymous usage telemetry, with an opt-out documented separately
